value.actual_behavior:
#68 moved to fixed at 2026-09-06T17:39:26 with all six of those null. It is 1
of 20 closed reports in the public tracker in that state; the other 19 carry
at least one. The check that covers this had been green since #53/#60 were
resolved and went red on today's sweep.
value.description:
Not disputing the fix itself -- something did change, and we can see it in the
data. The point is narrower: with all six fields empty there is nothing on the
record saying what was changed or who checked it, which is exactly what #53
and #60 were about and what the fix for them addressed. One line in
status_notes would have closed this and would also have answered the currency
question we filed as #70 without a round trip.
Nineteen of twenty closures do carry evidence, so this reads as one report
slipping through rather than the practice lapsing.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-tracker-closure-rate] 1 of 20 closed reports carry no evidence field at all (validated_at, triaged_at, severity_confirmed, ticket_url, fix_pr_url, status_notes)

  tests/rest/test_bounty_tracker.py::test_closures_in_the_public_tracker_carry_evidence

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: read-only
verification of the REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces. No
state-changing account action, no trading, no order placement, no deposit or
withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects are out of scope.
Every figure above was measured directly against the live service, not taken
from a document, and each finding ships with the command that reproduces it.
value.expected_behavior:

validated_at, triaged_at, severity_confirmed, ticket_url, fix_pr_url or
status_notes.
